articles.title: The Plan: With a Big Vacancy Looming, Durst Goes Big on Renovating 114 West 47th
articles.narrative: The Durst Organization is undertaking a significant renovation of its 26-story office building at 114 West 47th Street in Midtown Manhattan. The project, prompted by a major tenant's lease expiration in early 2028, aims to modernize the 600,000-square-foot asset with a new lobby, enhanced tenant amenities, private terraces, and updated building systems. The renovation is expected to be completed by 2029, positioning the property as a world-class work environment for visionary companies seeking a new headquarters in a prime Midtown location.

data_points.address: 114 West 47th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Building will feature private terraces on seven floors, ceiling heights between 12 and 14 feet, and floor plates ranging from 18,000 to 32,000 square feet. The lobby will extend into a 2,500-square-foot tenant lounge and conferencing center with a cafe area.
data_points.project_notes: Renovation prompted by a major tenant's lease expiration in early 2028. Existing office and retail tenants will remain during renovations.

articles.title: Bill Ackman Buys 125 West End Avenue for $260M Brain Research Institute
articles.narrative: The Pershing Square Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Bill Ackman's hedge fund, has acquired 125 West End Avenue for $188 million, with plans to establish a brain research institute. This acquisition is part of a larger $260 million initiative that includes an in-contract purchase of the neighboring 320 West 66th Street, aiming to create a 700,000-square-foot life sciences and office campus. The foundation is partnering with Mount Sinai Hospital System on the development of the research institute.

data_points.address: 125 West End Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The building, also known as West End Labs, is largely vacant and was previously part of the 3.4-acre West End Campus.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition is part of a larger $260 million plan to establish the Ackman Oxman Institute, a brain research center. The overall plan includes an in-contract sale for the neighboring 320 West 66th Street for approximately $70 million, bringing the total campus to an estimated 700,000 square feet. The West End Campus was previously sold to Taconic by Silverstein Properties for $230 million in 2019 and repositioned as a research and laboratory complex.

articles.title: Goulston & Storrs Adds Brian Grindall to Real Estate Practice
articles.narrative: Brian Grindall, a seasoned commercial real estate attorney, has joined Goulston & Storrs as a director in its Washington, D.C. office, bolstering the firm's real estate practice. Grindall brings over two decades of experience advising on a wide range of CRE transactions, including acquisitions, dispositions, financing, leasing, and development, as well as joint ventures and distressed property restructurings. His addition is expected to enhance the firm's capacity to handle complex real estate matters for its clients.

articles.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Takes 5K SF at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx
articles.narrative: Simone Development Companies has achieved full occupancy at its 27,275-square-foot medical and office building at 1733 Eastchester Road in the Bronx, following two recent lease agreements. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) signed a long-term, 5,234-square-foot lease on behalf of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for a new Bronx Vet Center. Additionally, Downtown Brooklyn Physical Therapy leased 2,766 square feet for its first Bronx location. The full lease-up underscores the increasing demand for high-quality outpatient medical and social services space in the Bronx, according to the landlord.

data_points.notable_features: Two-story building offering modern professional space with high visibility and a strategic location.

articles.title: Whole Foods Signs 8K-SF Lease to Open Daily Shop at 1524 Second Avenue
articles.narrative: Whole Foods Market has signed an 8,121-square-foot lease for a new small-format store, likely a 'Daily Shop' concept focusing on prepared foods, at 1524 Second Avenue in Manhattan's Upper East Side. The transaction secures a highly visible corner location in a well-established retail corridor with significant residential density, making it an ideal fit for the grocer's neighborhood store format. This lease reflects Whole Foods' strategy to expand its smaller-scale concepts in New York City.

data_points.address: 1524 Second Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Highly visible corner location in a well-established neighborhood retail corridor with surrounding residential density.

articles.title: Rockspring Underway on 254-Acre Mixed-Use Development in Marble Falls, Texas
articles.narrative: Rockspring, a Houston-based firm, is developing The Highlands, a 254-acre mixed-use project in Marble Falls, Texas. The master-planned community will feature single-family homes, apartments, townhomes, commercial space, and parks. The developer has secured a $28.2 million construction loan and is finalizing a public infrastructure development bond with the City of Marble Falls to fund predevelopment and sitework, which are expected to cost over $70 million.

articles.title: Core Spaces Breaks Ground on 1,656-Bed Student Housing Development Near University of Georgia
articles.narrative: Core Spaces has commenced construction on Hub Athens Dougherty, a substantial 1,656-bed student housing development near the University of Georgia. The project, slated for completion in 2028, will feature 536 units and a range of amenities. This development includes significant public benefit initiatives in partnership with Athens-Clarke County, such as a public parking deck, retail space, infrastructure upgrades to support affordable housing, and the preservation of historic buildings.

The newly built 93,352-square-foot retail center was sold by a repeat developer of grocery-anchored properties to Calhoun Shores LLC. articles.title: A nice surprise: Some good news for the Chicago area’s office market
articles.narrative: Metropolitan Chicago's office market experienced a positive shift in the second quarter, with both downtown and suburban areas recording strong positive net absorption, signaling a potential stabilization in tenant demand. Downtown Chicago saw over 1.08 million square feet of positive absorption, its best performance since early 2021, while the suburban market added another 605,806 square feet. This improvement is attributed to companies leasing more space in higher-quality buildings and a decrease in available sublease space, suggesting a cautious return to office commitments despite a slower economy and hybrid work models.
articles.market_intelligence: The suburban Chicago office market's vacancy rate fell to 26.1% from 26.6% a year ago. Class-A properties accounted for nearly three-quarters of the positive absorption in the suburbs and 55% of all leasing activity. Downtown Chicago's vacancy rate fell to 24.9% after reaching a record high in Q1 2026. Sublease space in downtown Chicago dropped to its lowest level since the pandemic began. Mid-sized suburban office buildings (20,000-100,000 SF) are outperforming the rest of the sector with consistent leasing activity and below-average vacancy rates. Office investment sales in the suburbs totaled $72.08 million across 11 properties in Q2 2026.

articles.title: Scannell Properties developing master-planned industrial park in Chambers County
articles.narrative: Scannell Properties has commenced construction on the first phase of Chambers99 Logistics Center, a master-planned industrial park in Chambers County, Texas. This initial phase includes two speculative industrial buildings totaling 491,400 square feet, with future phases potentially adding up to 1 million square feet. The development is strategically located along Highway 99, offering direct access to a key transportation corridor and proximity to Port Houston, making it attractive for bulk distribution, manufacturing, and packaging operations.

data_points.phase_1: two speculative industrial buildings totaling 491,400 square feet
data_points.total_project_all_phases: up to 1 million square feet of additional industrial space

Features include cross-dock and front-load configurations, 32-36 foot clear heights, ESFR sprinkler systems, and ample truck courts.
data_points.project_notes: First phase includes two speculative buildings: a 386,880 SF cross-dock facility and a 104,520 SF front-load facility. Future phases will include build-to-suit facilities.

The off-market transaction involved purchasing the property from the family of its original developer, who had owned and operated it for over six decades. Paragon plans to implement upgrades to the center's physical attributes, including common areas, building facades, lighting, and signage, while preserving its long-standing anchor tenants.

articles.title: Sterling Organization Nears Delivery of High-Bay Bronx Warehouse
articles.narrative: Sterling Organization is nearing delivery of 307 Bruckner, a newly developed 100,000-square-foot industrial property in the Bronx, with JLL leading the marketing efforts. The facility is designed to meet the evolving needs of companies serving the New York market, offering features like high-bay warehousing and covered fleet parking to enhance supply chain efficiency and shorten delivery windows. Its strategic location provides rapid connectivity to a large population base across multiple boroughs and northern New Jersey.

The transaction underscores the sustained demand for high-quality industrial space in Orange County, particularly within the resilient Airport Area industrial market.

articles.title: Clarion Partners Acquires Grocery-Anchored Fairfield County Retail

This acquisition aligns with Clarion's strategy to invest in well-located, grocery-anchored retail centers that offer stable cash flow and long-term value, benefiting from strong occupancy and a strategic location in an affluent market.

articles.title: How A New Financing Model Helps Spur More Mixed-Income Housing
articles.narrative: A new report from the Urban Institute highlights MassHousing's Bringing Innovation to Lending and Development (BILD) program as a promising model for spurring mixed-income housing development. The program, which uses public funds as both debt and equity, aims to fill capital stack gaps for projects stalled by high interest rates and construction costs. MassHousing has already committed $31 million in equity and over $189 million in debt through the program, funding six projects totaling 605 units. The BILD program's innovative approach, including a subordinate loan and preferred equity with lower return requirements, helps mitigate risk for lenders and makes projects financially feasible while maintaining affordability.

articles.title: Lineage Fined For Rotting Food, Swarms Of Flies At Burned LA Cold Storage Warehouse
articles.narrative: Lineage Logistics is facing daily fines and community backlash due to unsanitary conditions at its 500,000-square-foot cold storage warehouse in Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, which suffered a major fire in June. Residents are reporting pervasive odors from rotting food and an infestation of flies and rats, prompting calls for a mandatory evacuation. The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health has cited Lineage for nuisance conditions, imposing a $500 daily fine until the issues are resolved. The City of Los Angeles has mandated that Lineage remove all spoiled food by August 14, threatening legal action if the deadline is not met.

articles.title: Mamdani Adds Millions To Program Helping Retailers Negotiate With Landlords
articles.narrative: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has doubled the funding for a city program that provides legal assistance to commercial tenants in lease negotiations, increasing the allocation from $4 million to $8 million. The program, run by the Department of Small Business Services, helps small businesses navigate rising rents and competitive market conditions by offering support for new leases, renewals, terminations, and disputes. Industry professionals note that the program benefits both tenants by providing crucial guidance and landlords by ensuring more capable and informed negotiation partners, ultimately streamlining the leasing process in a tight retail market.

articles.market_intelligence: Average retail availability in New York City's nine prime corridors was 11.9% at the end of Q1, the lowest quarterly rate recorded by JLL since Q3 2017. This lack of available space is driving tenants to side streets. articles.title: Proptech Firm Dwelly Raises $170M For Its AI-Forward Acquisition Plan
articles.narrative: Proptech firm Dwelly has secured $170 million in new financing, comprising $95 million in equity and a $75 million debt facility, to fuel its acquisition strategy. The UK-based company, founded in 2023, specializes in acquiring small property management and brokerage firms, integrating their databases, and leveraging AI to enhance operational efficiency and reduce costs. This capital infusion will enable Dwelly to expand its portfolio of acquired listing companies, which currently manages 15,000 properties and generates $466 million in annual rent. The firm's approach, which includes using AI agents to manage a higher volume of units and streamline tasks like maintenance requests, reflects a broader industry trend among multifamily operators seeking to optimize efficiency amidst rising costs and flatlining property incomes.
